key_insight: The paper reframes medical agents as sequential decision systems and argues that progress should be driven by deployment-ready clinical environments, not just bigger models.
clinical_relevance: It offers a roadmap for safer AI in radiology and other workflows by emphasizing assisted-to-autonomous operation, tool use, and interactive training in real hospital systems.
method: Defines medical agents with a 3-level autonomy taxonomy: assisted, cooperative, fully autonomous
Organizes the field into framework scaling, capability scaling, and environment scaling
Highlights clinical gyms and integrations with PACS, EHR, and FHIR as key training/evaluation settings
evidence_signal: The review synthesizes more than 300 references and emphasizes contamination-resistant benchmarks and interactive environments for evaluating real-world readiness.
watch_item: Autonomy increases the risk of hallucination, cascading failures, and fairness issues, so clinical deployment needs careful oversight and validation.
paper_title: The Path to Self-Evolving Clinical Systems: Scaling Medical Agents from Assistance to Autonomy
